scope: Theorem 1.1 of the manuscript “Unconditional time lower bounds for Weisfeiler–Leman equivalence” (preprints/Unconditional-time-lower-bounds-for-Weisfeiler-Leman-equivalence-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 133 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 5d58d0f7cee1b9ed), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 1-2. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There are absolute constants c > 0 and k0 with the following property. For every fixed integer k ≥ k0 and every correct deterministic decider A for k-Weisfeiler–Leman equivalence, there is an integer n0 = n0(A, k) such that TA(n) ≥ nck for every integer n ≥ n0. This holds for multitape Turing machines and for sequential random-access machines with O(log(n + 2))-bit addresses and words, boundedly many memory accesses per instruction, and fixed instructions 1 computable in time polynomial in the word length. The same bound holds if A is required to decide correctly only on pairs of simple connected uncolored graphs of diameter at most two, with TA(n) maximized over that class. It applies both to the joint replacement-multiset convention for k-dimensional refinement and to the separate-multiset convention defined below.
